cards.d: To allot something means to give it to someone.
cards.e: The coach allotted each team five minutes to prepare a strategy.
cards.ielts: Many governments allot a significant share of their annual budget to healthcare, yet waiting lists in public hospitals continue to grow.

cards.d: To appall means to horrify, shock, or disgust someone.
cards.e: The boy was appalled when he saw the accident.
cards.ielts: Many citizens were appalled by reports that factories had been dumping toxic waste directly into the river for years.

cards.d: A cache is a hiding place for valuable things.
cards.e: The pirates kept their jewelry in a cache hidden in a cave.
cards.ielts: Police discovered a cache of stolen electronics in an abandoned warehouse on the outskirts of the city.

cards.d: Convenience is a state of being able to do something with little effort.
cards.e: The Internet allows consumers to shop at their own convenience.
cards.ielts: Online banking offers great convenience, but older people often struggle to use these services without help from younger relatives.

cards.d: A dearth is an amount or supply which is not large enough.
cards.e: There is a dearth of money in my bank account. I can’t afford a new car.
cards.ielts: Rural schools in many developing countries suffer from a dearth of qualified teachers, which widens the gap between urban and rural pupils.

cards.d: If a thing you do is deliberate, you intend to do it.
cards.e: She made a deliberate effort to save money each month.
cards.ielts: Some critics argue that the deliberate spread of false information online poses a serious threat to democratic elections.

cards.d: When something is dire, it is terrible and very serious.
cards.e: The tornado created a dire situation for the small town.
cards.ielts: Without urgent action on carbon emissions, scientists warn that low-lying coastal nations will face dire consequences within decades.

cards.d: To elapse means to pass, as in seconds, minutes, or hours.
cards.e: A few seconds must elapse before you can take another picture.
cards.ielts: Once two years have elapsed since graduation, many young people find that their university knowledge no longer matches what employers need.

cards.d: Empathy is sharing or understanding another person’s feelings.
cards.e: The caring nurse had empathy for her patients.
cards.ielts: Teachers who show empathy towards struggling students tend to create classrooms where young people feel safe enough to ask questions.

cards.d: When something is fanciful, it is unusual or unrealistic.
cards.e: The girl had fanciful ideas about doing well in school without studying.
cards.ielts: The idea that robots will replace every teacher by 2030 seems rather fanciful, since learning depends heavily on human interaction.

cards.d: To gripe means to complain constantly.
cards.e: Lawrence always gripes when he has to do chores.
cards.ielts: Commuters frequently gripe about overcrowded trains, but few of them are willing to pay higher fares for better services.

cards.d: When something is grueling, it is very hard to do.
cards.e: The climber faced the grueling task of reaching the top of the steep mountain.
cards.ielts: Junior doctors often work grueling shifts of more than twelve hours, which can affect both their health and the quality of patient care.

cards.d: When something is mundane, it is boring, common, or ordinary.
cards.e: The man had the mundane chore of raking thousands of leaves into piles.
cards.ielts: Automation is likely to take over mundane tasks such as data entry, allowing employees to focus on more creative work.

cards.d: To opt is to make a choice, especially when deciding in favor of something.
cards.e: My brother likes chocolate ice cream, but I always opt for vanilla.
cards.ielts: An increasing number of young families opt for public transport rather than buying a car, mainly because of rising fuel prices.

cards.d: Outrage is a very strong emotion of anger or shock.
cards.e: Tommy was feeling outrage when his parents said he couldn’t go to the dance.
cards.ielts: The decision to close the local library caused widespread outrage among residents who relied on it for free internet access.

cards.d: When an amount of something is paltry, it is very small.
cards.e: The poor man had a paltry sum of money.
cards.ielts: Many interns are paid a paltry salary that barely covers their rent, which discourages talented students from poorer backgrounds.

cards.d: To rectify something means to correct it.
cards.e: I quickly rectified the spelling mistakes that I had on my essay.
cards.ielts: The government has promised to rectify the shortage of affordable housing by building fifty thousand new homes over the next five years.

cards.d: When someone is resourceful, they are good at dealing with hard situations.
cards.e: After his boat sunk, Matt was resourceful enough to build a raft.
cards.ielts: Children who are given some independence often become more resourceful adults, able to solve problems without constant guidance.

cards.d: Sustenance is food and water needed to keep a person, animal, or plant alive.
cards.e: Without the proper sustenance, the man will starve.
cards.ielts: In many rural areas, small family farms remain the main source of sustenance for millions of people.

cards.d: When something is tedious, it is long, frustrating, and boring.
cards.e: His job involved a lot of tedious typing, filing, and organizing.
cards.ielts: In my opinion, the most tedious part of learning a language is memorising grammar rules, so I prefer practising through conversation.
